en: The Pasig River actually flows in the opposite direction, from Laguna de Bay out to Manila Bay.
Despite its nickname monkey-eating eagle, the Philippine eagle primarily hunts flying squirrels and giant cloud rats, not monkeys.
Geologically, the Palawan mainland is part of the Asian continental shelf rather than the volcanic Philippine archipelago.
The Chocolate Hills turn brown during the dry season because the grass covering these limestone mounds dries up.
The lower portion of the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River is actually influenced by ocean tides and contains brackish water.
Mayon Volcano's perfectly symmetrical cone shape is formed by alternating layers of hardened lava and volcanic ash, not solid granite.
The Philippines has two distinct seasons due to its tropical monsoon climate, despite being located several degrees north of the equator.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, while Lake Lanao is only the second largest.
The Banaue Rice Terraces are entirely man-made, carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people over two thousand years ago.
The Sibuyan Sea actually lies between the islands of Luzon and the Visayas, not between Luzon and Mindanao.
Taal Volcano's main crater is actually a lake that contains its own smaller island called Vulcan Point.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is located in the middle of the Sulu Sea, far from the Palawan mainland.
